newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia's Sihanouk asks Hun Sen to pursue peace.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Sihanouk asks Hun Sen to pursue peace.

text.p: Cambodia's King Norodom Sihanouk said on Wednesday he has asked Second Prime Minister Hun Sen to end violence in Cambodia and work towards national reconciliation.

The king, in his first comments since a five-hour meeting with Hun Sen and a high-level Cambodian delegation in Beijing on Tuesday, also called for the country's constitution and human rights to be respected.

"I asked all of them to try to make an effort to achieve peace, cool down the situation and end war, insecurity and violence," Sihanouk said in a statement from his residence in Beijing, where he is receiving medical treatment.
The statement was also released by the palace in Phnom Penh.

The king said he had asked Hun Sen and newly-appointed First Prime Minister Ung Huot "to somehow achieve non-violence, national reconciliation, peaceful co-existence, solidarity, mutual respect, respect for human rights and our national constitution".
Hun Sen overthrew his original co-prime minister, the king's son, Prince Norodom Ranariddh, on July 6 and later supported Ung Huot's nomination to take his place.
A Cambodian military court has since issued a warrant for Ranariddh's arrest on charges of weapons smuggling.
Political analysts in Phnom Penh said Hun Sen would seek approval for his new government in his meeting with the king.

But last week Sihanouk, expressing strong disapproval of recent events in his country, called Ung Huot a "puppet" of Hun Sen and said he was dismayed by what had happened in Cambodia. He likened the situation to a "comedy".

In his statement on Wednesday, Sihanouk did not provide any other details of Tuesday's meeting nor did he mention an offer to abdicate made shortly before Hun Sen and his colleagues left Phnom Penh to meet him in the Chinese capital.
The king earlier said he wanted any negotiations on Cambodia's future to be held in secret.

A brief statement from the government delegation issued by the Ministry of Information in Phnom Penh said Sihanouk had asked the delegation to assure Cambodians that the king was "working with all the people in the country".
It also said Sihanouk would visit the northern town of Siem Reap "in the near future".
On Monday Sihanouk, who has been in Beijing since February, said he would soon visit Siem Reap, home to the famed temple complex of Angkor, to hold a Buddhist ceremony for peace and reconciliation.

The Cambodian delegation also met China's First Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Tang Jiaxuan, who was quoted in the statement as saying that recent events in Cambodia were an internal affair and Cambodia was able to solve its own problems.
The Cambodian government delegation, which arrived in Beijing on Monday, was scheduled to return to Phnom Penh on Thursday.
